stem: Earbuds have an own-price elasticity of -1.6. A manager says: "Demand is elastic, so we can never raise the price." What is wrong with this?

options.text: Nothing: with elastic demand, any price rise always loses the business money
Revenue falls, but profit can still rise if each unit earns enough more
With an elasticity of -1.6, a price rise raises revenue and profit
Elasticity only describes price cuts, never price rises
